h1.text: On January 1st, 2027, California bans Red No. 3 in food, with no sell-through period.

h2.text: This is a simulated compliance drill on 20 California Walmart and Sam's Club locations, where the dye hides under names like erythrosine and E127.

h3.text: You'll see a working system that Gemini 4 Argon wrote this morning, in one generation.

c1.text: Here's the drill. We run the core on all 20 stores: 13,746 shelf tasks, replayed overnight against the midnight deadline. Each dot turns green when its store is done.

c2.text: Click a Supercenter and you're inside it. Flashing tags are pulls still pending. Associates walk to each facing, pull the product, and place a substitute.

c3.text: Every verdict carries its evidence. Erythrosine: caught and pulled. A vague "artificial color": held to verify. A Red 40 decoy: kept on the shelf.

c4.text: Then the verifier. Argon's unedited core: 350 hard errors, and recall 0.947. It missed 25 products spelled like "F D and C" with spaces, or Spanish "rojo".

c5.text: After 3 small logged patches: 0 hard errors, recall 1.0, precision 0.998, and 0 of 483 decoys pulled.

c6.text: Stores, stock and staffing are simulated. Every number came from the verifier.
